evidence.title: UN food agency official fired after highlighting Gaza hunger

occurrences.checkable_against: The New Humanitarian interview with Benjamin Davis
occurrences.quote_span: He said in an interview with The New Humanitarian that he wished some of the FAO’s senior management had attended the moments of silence and “step up.”

occurrences.checkable_against: The New Humanitarian interview with Benjamin Davis
occurrences.quote_span: “But I tell people –– because a lot of people are bummed out, they don’t know what to do, they’re very disheartened –– I say, just do whatever little you can do,” he told the outlet.

occurrences.subject: Benjamin Davis

occurrences.checkable_against: Benjamin Davis's official response to FAO dismissal
occurrences.quote_span: Davis wrote in his official response to his dismissal that silence “in the face of suffering and injustice is not neutrality, it is complicity.”

occurrences.subject: Benjamin Davis

occurrences.checkable_against: Reuters interview with Benjamin Davis

occurrences.checkable_against: FAO disciplinary records and Reuters interview with Benjamin Davis
occurrences.quote_span: “I’ve been disciplined without due process for speaking about a subject at the core of FAO’s mandate about the right to food which is the most basic of human rights.”
occurrences.speaker: Benjamin Davis
occurrences.subject: Benjamin Davis

occurrences.checkable_against: Benjamin Davis's letter responding to his dismissal
occurrences.quote_span: “Being true to our mandate calls for a frank and open discussion around starvation, famine, and genocide in Palestine and elsewhere.”

occurrences.subject: Benjamin Davis

occurrences.checkable_against: FAO personnel records and Benjamin Davis employment and work records
occurrences.quote_span: Former United Nations food agency official Benjamin Davis said he was fired after his work, including briefs and seminars, highlighted the hunger crisis in Gaza, The Guardian reported Tuesday.
occurrences.speaker: Benjamin Davis
occurrences.subject: Benjamin Davis

occurrences.checkable_against: The Guardian interview with Benjamin Davis
occurrences.quote_span: He accused Qu of making comments about human rights that undermine “the foundations of why we’re here basically, or why FAO is part of the United Nations and why the United Nations exists.”
occurrences.speaker: Benjamin Davis
occurrences.subject: Benjamin Davis

occurrences.checkable_against: Benjamin Davis's letter responding to his dismissal
occurrences.quote_span: “Shutting down discussion on the starvation of the Palestinian people weakens the reputation of the organisation and the legitimacy of our mandate,” his letter reads, according to The Guardian.
occurrences.speaker: Benjamin Davis
occurrences.subject: Benjamin Davis

occurrences.checkable_against: FAO personnel records and Qu Dongyu's written request to Benjamin Davis
occurrences.quote_span: FAO Director-General Qu Dongyu requested Davis, a Spanish American citizen and a 26-year fixture within the FAO, step down from his role by Sept. 30.
occurrences.speaker: The Guardian's report as relayed by The Hill
